clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old Caucasian female with no past medical history presented with right-sided neck pain on day 1, followed by erythematous vesicular rash in C2-C4 dermatomes (right anterior chest, neck, shoulder) appearing on day 4. The rash was initially misdiagnosed as contact dermatitis at a walk-in clinic. By day 12, she developed right ear discomfort and hearing difficulty with rash extending to the auricle. On day 14, she woke with partial right-sided facial paralysis. She was evaluated in the Emergency Room where Ramsay Hunt Syndrome was diagnosed. Antiviral therapy (valacyclovir extended to 10 days) and corticosteroid therapy (prednisone) were initiated, and a neuro-ophthalmology referral was made. By day 46, she showed significant clinical improvement with symmetric smile and complete right eye closure.
